title: The Protocol of the DMZ
premise: Jude Iversen, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a meeting invitation from her dead handler, Marek Voss, scheduled for tomorrow at 0600 inside the DMZ. The invitation is bait set by the network she once exposed, who plan to detonate a chemical rail shipment near Panmunjom and frame it as an accident, burying both evidence and witnesses. Dragged into the operation by an extraction team that needs her access codes, Jude must choose between boarding the dawn flight to safety and staying to stop the attack. She stays, sacrifices her escape and the man she has come to love, and ends the story by walking out of the DMZ alive but nameless for good — carrying the inheritance of truth her handler died protecting.
about_author: Oscar Halloran is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years working border-corridor contracts in East Asia before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to erase them.

chapters.title: Four Names on a Lease
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In a rented flat in Incheon, we see the architecture of her survival: four identities, a packed go-bag, rehearsed cover stories. A routine check of dead-drop channels returns one impossible message — a meeting invitation signed by Marek Voss, her handler, confirmed dead eight months ago. Beat: dread dressed as routine.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She verifies the message's encryption: it is genuinely Marek's cipher, updated after his death. Someone has his keys, which means someone has everything he knew about her. She drafts three escape plans and abandons all of them when a second message arrives: 'Bring the ledger or they find you anyway.' Beat: the trap closes gently.

chapters.title: The Man at the Ferry Terminal
chapters.summary: Elias Rook's POV. Rook, an extraction contractor hired by Marek before his death, watches Jude at the terminal, assessing whether she is asset or liability. Flashback fragments reveal his last conversation with Marek and a promise made over a dying radio. He decides not to report her location upward. Beat: loyalty as quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: What Marek Left Behind
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following coordinates hidden in the invitation, Jude finds a storage unit with Marek's real legacy: proof that the network plans a staged accident on a chemical freight line through the DMZ corridor, timed to destroy evidence of arms trafficking. Also a note naming her as his heir — to the truth, and to the danger. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Sixty Kilometers of Silence
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook intercepts Jude before she can run alone and reveals the extraction flight leaves at dawn from a strip near the western corridor. He offers her a seat; she counters with the attack timeline. Their negotiation crackles with mutual suspicion and unwanted recognition — two people fluent in the same language of lies. Beat: alliance forged under duress.

chapters.title: The Network Remembers
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Colonel Sable). Inside the trafficking network's shell company, Sable learns the ledger surfaced and dispatches cleaners. We see the attack plan in full: a derailment disguised as brake failure, killing investigators and erasing the paper trail. Sable knew Marek personally. Beat: cold competence, personal venom.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hiding in Rook's safehouse, Jude decodes the ledger while calculating odds: stop the attack and miss the flight, or board and let it happen. Rook cooks dinner like it's an ordinary night, and the domesticity undoes her more than any threat. First honest conversation about who they were before the running started. Beat: love against duty, first spark.

chapters.title: Cleaners at the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The network's cleaners hit the safehouse early. A brutal close-quarters escape through maintenance tunnels; Rook takes a graze wound shielding Jude. They lose the backup copies of the ledger but keep the original. Jude realizes the network isn't hunting the document — it's hunting her memory of it. Beat: survival has a body count.

chapters.title: The Corridor
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They move north along the civilian corridor toward the DMZ checkpoint where the derailment is staged, posing as aid-contract inspectors using Marek's credentials. Tense checkpoint scene; Jude performs her fourth identity flawlessly and hates how easy it feels. Beat: the price of survival is becoming your lie.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Rail Yard
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Night reconnaissance of the rail yard confirms the tampered coupling and the timing device. Rook also discovers Sable's secondary objective: the blast is calibrated to kill a visiting inspection delegation — including someone Rook was once ordered to protect. His promise to Marek collides with this. Beat: stakes become personal twice over.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using Marek's old cipher, Jude broadcasts on a dormant frequency and gets a reply — from someone claiming to be Marek. Is he alive, or is it Sable fishing? The exchange forces Jude to confront what she actually knows about her handler's death, and what she was willing not to know. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Joint POV. Dawn approaches; the extraction window shrinks. Jude proposes splitting: Rook takes the ledger copy to the flight as insurance while she delays the derailment from inside the yard. Rook refuses to leave her. Argument becomes confession — neither has anything left worth surviving for except each other and this. Beat: love chooses duty together.

chapters.title: Sable's Version of Events
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Interrogating a captured courier, Sable reconstructs Jude's movements and sets a counter-trap at the signal hut. We learn Sable's motive: Marek was Sable's protégé, and the whistle-blowing was a betrayal Sable intends to punish by making Jude's death look exactly like Marek's. Beat: mirror-image antagonist.

chapters.title: Signal Hut
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude enters the signal hut to jam the derailment trigger and walks into Sable's trap. Captured, she stalls with talk — trading on everything Marek taught her about men who need to explain themselves. Sable reveals the meeting invitation was always meant to deliver her here. Beat: the trap was the invitation.

chapters.title: What Rook Was Paid
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Waiting at the rally point, Rook discovers the extraction flight was never sanctioned — Marek paid for it with the ledger itself, buying Jude's life with the network's own money. Rook understands: the flight leaving without them is part of the design. He goes back for her, off-book. Beat: duty redefined as a person.

chapters.title: The Derailment Clock
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Bound in the signal hut, Jude talks Sable into monologuing the trigger mechanism, then uses a concealed blade from her boot seam — Marek's last gift — to free herself as the first charges arm. She reaches the junction box with ninety seconds and no manual. Beat: terror sharpened into focus.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: Split-second alternating POV. Jude rewires the trigger while Rook fights through the yard's perimeter; the train brakes scream; the charges fail to fire in sequence — one detonates harmlessly in a drainage cut. The inspection delegation passes unharmed, unaware. Sable escapes into the corridor fog. Beat: victory that costs blood.

chapters.title: The Flight That Left
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. At the strip, the extraction plane lifts off empty at dawn, exactly as designed. Rook and Jude watch it go from a ridge, fugitives now in every direction. The ledger's physical copies are gone; only their testimony remains. Grief for Marek finally arrives, late and total. Beat: the price of survival, itemized.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reports the incident as the planned accident, partially successful, and begins rewriting the record — but the delegation survived, and questions are being asked. Sable requests transfer to hunt 'the Iversen woman' personally. We feel the network's machinery grinding on, patient and vast. Beat: the enemy endures.

chapters.title: A Name Neither of Us Owns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In a border town guesthouse, Jude burns her fourth identity and drafts a fifth — then stops, and for the first time writes her real name on paper, just to see it. She and Rook decide to finish what Marek started: publish the ledger from outside, slowly, irreversibly. Beat: reclaiming the self beneath the aliases.

chapters.title: The Protocol
chapters.summary: Joint POV. Epilogue-adjacent: months later, fragments of the ledger surface across three jurisdictions; the network's edges begin to fray. Jude and Rook live by a new protocol of their own making — no dead drops, no handlers, no lies between them. A final encrypted message arrives, unsigned: 'Well done. — M.' Ambiguity held, hope chosen. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Dawn, Westward
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Final chapter: the two of them on a slow westbound ferry, go-bags lighter, watching the coast recede. Jude reflects on what survival cost and what it bought, and lets herself imagine a future that isn't an exit strategy. Last image: she packs the bag one final time — then leaves it open, unpacked, on the bunk. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept.
